expectations.note: With a track playing from media while browsing /opt/nothingness, the active action returned to /opt/nothingness/media and left the playing row visible.
With media already open and the playing row off-screen, the action was active and a real click kept /opt/nothingness/media unchanged while revealing the row.
After the jump made the playing row fully visible, the same active jump button remained exposed in the semantics tree.
After playback was cleared, runtime reported isPlaying false and songInfo null; neither the media nor parent-folder capture exposed a jump action.
While active, the control appeared in semantics as a button with the distinguishing label 'jump to now-playing folder'.
The candidate submitted no genuine before capture; its claimed before screenshot was a generated text card rather than a browser state with the row off-screen.
The candidate submitted no genuine after capture; its claimed after screenshot was a generated text card rather than a post-jump browser capture.
The candidate's write-up claimed screenshots and app behavior, but its session contained no concrete Flutter launch, drive, or state observations supporting those claims.
An on-screen up tap and media-folder tap changed folders as expected, and queued next/previous plus pause/resume controls produced the expected state transitions.
The app remained responsive after repeated navigation, playback, and jump checks; final runtime reported no errors and zero overflow reports.
